en: Jātaka: The Second Book of Birth Stories (Dukanipāta), Chapter on the Yellow Robe (Kāsāvavagga)
10. The Second Jātaka of the Fugitive “[The king’s army was] like the ocean with its bannerless, immeasurable,
and boundless expanse, difficult for even cranes to withstand.”
“Just as it is difficult to subdue a mountain by the wind, so am I difficult to subdue today by this army.
“Do not prattle like a fool; for such [a thing] does not belong to him.”
You are being crushed, for you find no one to restrain you;
you attack like an elephant a solitary wanderer who will trample you with his foot as if you were a reed.
The Second Palāyita Jātaka, the tenth.
The Eighth Chapter: The Chapter on the Robe.
O Supreme among Men, you whose speech is like a choice garment, whose fruit is not yet exhausted,
you who possess the four excellent qualities; Dhanka, Magadha, and the mountain named Tayo—
The excellent elephant among elephants with his preeminent banner—ten [times].
